findings.name: A high-priority task was held up by lower-priority work
findings.impact: The most urgent part of your program waits for work that should never delay it, so it can miss its deadline even though the CPU had time for it.
findings.summary: control (prio 50) was blocked 5.19 ms on a semaphore released by logger (prio 10); for 5.19 ms of that, logger was ready but telemetry (prio 20) held its CPU. Seen 200x.
findings.qnx: QNX semaphores have no owner, so the kernel cannot apply priority inheritance. A pthread mutex (priority inheritance is the QNX default) would have boosted logger to priority 50 and the medium-priority work could not have preempted it.

findings.name: A periodic task finished late
findings.impact: The task did not complete within its time budget. This is what users and safety checks notice.
findings.summary: 'control' missed its 2000 us budget in 200 of 200 jobs (measured from release); worst response 5.32 ms (2.7x budget); p99 release jitter 0.13 ms, worst job: 0.00 ms late wake-up, 0.01 ms waiting for the CPU, 5.19 ms blocked, 0.12 ms running.
findings.qnx: Response measured from the job's release (TL_RELEASE marker or the period grid) to TL_JOB_END, so wake-up latency before the job starts counts against the budget.

radar.name: control
radar.summary: control (prio 50) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 100 of its 100 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 2000 ms. It stands out in: time blocked on a semaphore (higher than healthy), time blocked while a lower-priority thread held its CPU (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is priority inversion through a semaphore used as a lock (distance 0.3, inside the 0.917 typical for that pattern).

remedies.title: Replace semaphore 'buf_lock' (used as a lock) with a priority-inheriting mutex
remedies.rationale: A POSIX semaphore has no owner, so the QNX kernel cannot raise the priority of the thread that holds it: a medium-priority thread preempts the holder and the high-priority waiter waits for both. A pthread mutex has an owner; with PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT (the QNX default) the holder runs at the waiter's priority until it unlocks.

remedies.title: Deadline misses in 'control': a symptom
remedies.rationale: deadline miss is the visible effect; the trace also shows its cause (priority_inversion). It is expected to clear with that fix, and the re-trace checks that it does.
